title: Basic 1 · Rotate an image
summary: Wire a Rotate node after the Clock test image, set angle_deg, and run. The basic drag → wire → param → Run cycle in one lesson.

steps.title: Try rotation
steps.body: This first tutorial walks through the core pyspider_web cycle — **drop a data node → drop an operation node → wire them → set a param → Run** — with the **Rotate** operation on a clock-face test image.

steps.title: Drop the data node
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Test · Clock face** onto the canvas. A clock-face image is easy to visually track under rotation — you can see at a glance where each hour tick moved.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph to execute the pipeline so far. You can inspect the image the `data.clock` node emits before moving on.

steps.title: Drop the Rotate node
steps.body: From Geometry, drag **Rotate** onto the canvas. Placing it next to the Clock keeps the wire tidy.

steps.title: Wire Clock → Rotate
steps.body: Drag from Clock's `image` output (right edge) to Rotate's `image` input (left edge). The wire lights up once the connection is valid.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph again. With `angle_deg` still at its default 0, Rotate is an identity pass-through, so the output matches the Clock input — a baseline to compare against after you set an angle.

steps.title: Click Rotate
steps.body: Click the Rotate node. The right Inspector reveals `angle_deg`, `cval`, and `interpolation`. `angle_deg` is the rotation in degrees (positive = counter-clockwise); `interpolation` picks the spline kind (default cubic).

steps.title: Set angle_deg to 45
steps.body: Enter **45** in `angle_deg`. The clock face will rotate 45° counter-clockwise.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. Clock → Rotate flows and the rotated clock appears on the Rotate node's preview.

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body: You now have the core workflow: drag from Palette → wire → set a param → Run. Changing `angle_deg` re-runs immediately. The next tutorial, **Basic 2 · Shift an image**, applies the same cycle to translation with the Shift node.
